trajectory_summary: The customer arrived warm and self-motivated, and stayed engaged through three separate site proposals even after being told the primary location wouldn't work. The rep, however, DQ'd the lead almost entirely off a Google Maps satellite view within the first two minutes and never captured a single verify-section item (bill, utility company, interest reason, co-owner) before ending the call. Energy leaked steadily as the customer kept offering solutions and the rep kept closing doors with the same underlying rationale.
outcome_dispute: This should be tagged dq (roof/shade), which the v1 tag likely reflects, but the manner of the DQ is questionable: it was made solely off satellite imagery ('it's just kinda hard to see because on Google Maps, all the trees are in the way') rather than any bill data, utility info, or even asking about specific sun-hours on the customer's actual property. A same-day satellite photo cannot reliably show winter sun angles, which the customer explicitly raised at 02:20-02:27. The DQ may be premature rather than earned.

observed_outcome.reasoning: The rep disqualified the property on shade grounds and the call ended with no appointment, no bill data, and no next step — a clean DQ outcome, though the grounds for the DQ (satellite imagery alone) are questionable per the trajectory_verdict.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The call never reached the bill_amount portion of the verify section; the rep moved straight from address confirmation into a shade-based DQ conversation and the call ended without any bill or usage figure discussed.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep never raised getting the utility bill in any form; the call was consumed entirely by address/shade verification before ending.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked what interested the customer in solar. The customer's opening line ('I was just reading about y'all') hints at self-driven research interest, but the rep did not explore it further, moving directly into address verification instead.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: Premature DQ from unverified satellite imagery
primary_coaching_focus.quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work
primary_coaching_focus.why: The rep disqualified a warm, self-motivated lead within the first 70 seconds of the call based solely on a Google Maps image the rep later admits is obstructed ('it's just kinda hard to see because on Google Maps, all the trees are in the way'), without asking a single qualifying question about actual sun hours or seasonal exposure, and without capturing bill, utility, or interest data. This is the single most consequential gap on the call — a motivated lead who proposed three separate site alternatives was let go without a real assessment.

key_moments.quote: So to be honest, Tracy, I do think that you don't have enough sun for solely for solar to work
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep disqualifies the property off a satellite image alone, before any verify items were captured. There is no shade/tree-coverage criterion defined in dq_rules today — this is a schema gap Ion needs to formalize (what counts as disqualifying shade, and what evidence standard is required before telling a customer their home won't work).

This undercuts the confidence of the initial disqualification and should have prompted the rep to ask the customer directly about sun exposure rather than relying on a visual the rep just admitted was obstructed.

key_moments.stewart_read: The customer hands the rep a specific, useful data point about seasonal sun exposure that directly counters the shade concern. The rep responds with a flat 'Mhmm. Okay' and then restates the same shade conclusion without engaging the point.

key_moments.stewart_read: This is the customer's third independent attempt to find a workable location on her property (main roof, garage, side yard) — a level of persistence and motivation that most leads never show. The rep's response pivots straight to a ground-mount cost explanation without first asking whether a roof-mount was possible on that side of the house.
